ratings_why.fun: Building a tree (tiny root, a blooming ivy, a crowd copying it) is a real puzzle every turn, held back from 8 only by how much bookkeeping the vines ask the player to track.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because it is a parasite layer that turns every other tribe's growth into its own, and Bloom flips it so a small host is the prize; no tribe today plays like that.

verdict_why: The engine is rich and should stay hot, but the no-loops rule and what happens when a host dies are only in the rationale, not on the cards.

points.text: Put the no-loops rule into Climb. As written, Lady Hedera's Start of Turn re-host or Traveller's Joy can make A climb B while B climbs A, and with full share that gain never ends.
Write in Climb what happens when a host dies or leaves (the rationale says it falls onto the biggest unit next to it). Old Man's Beard triggers on falling, and players can't read that from any card.

Say on Dodder Thread that climbers on it stay on it while it climbs the enemy. Then a whole tree hangs off an enemy for the fight and copies its Start of Combat buffs, which is the best trick in the tribe.
Hanger-on's condition is nearly always met in a Grand Oak. Paying more for a host with many climbers, or for a small blooming root, would make it a choice.
A second Lady Hedera does nothing. It could add a second re-host at Start of Combat, so the chain can jump to a fresh host mid-setup.

standouts.why: Lattice Ivy is a junction that changes the shape of the whole tree, and it combos with Cousin Dodder's stolen stats.
Mistletoe Clump does three jobs: drains a host into a Bloom root, grows itself, and hollows out a unit you plan to sell.
Old Man's Beard turns the tribe's main weakness, the host dying, into a payoff.

weakest.why: Barley-sugar Twiner is a plain host buff; it works only because the keyword copies it.
Ivy Sprig is a one-off +1/+1 with nothing to decide.
Missel just picks the obvious biggest tree; there is no decision it creates.

flags.note: Full share on every climber plus Lattice Ivy and Viscum's board-wide buff (which each climber gets directly and copies again) could stack fast.
A huge host dying early hands a third of it to every climber; the designer already names a cap.
Two hosts at Tier 1, four when golden, copies from the two biggest units late in the game.
Does Dodder Thread leave its friendly host when it climbs the enemy, and do its own climbers copy the enemy's gains?
When Mistletoe Clump takes 1/1 from its host, do the host's other climbers lose the stats they copied ("for as long as the host keeps them")?
